utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we continue, I'd like to put on the record two short matters. First, the Prosecution has made submissions concerning Witness RM070. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I ask myself whether we had to move into private session but I don't think there's any need for that. There were some issues raised on the 23rd of September, in relation to this witness. For the clarity of the record, the Chamber allows the Prosecution to proceed as suggested. That is, mainly in relation to the three issues that needed an answer. The fourth one has been resolved, meanwhile, by agreement among the parties. Then the second issue I'd like to briefly deal with is ... that we are still waiting for the result of the discussions the parties have had in relation to P15, which is MFI'd for the time being, and the Chamber would like to receive an update, still, this week. These two matters having ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to add, P15, there was an issue about the translation of that document -- English translation. Having dealt with those matters, we turn into closed session in order to hear the remainder of the testimony of the present witness. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We take a break, and we'll resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the opportunity for -- to deal with some associated exhibits related to the testimony of Witness John Clark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In relation to Witness John Clark, the Chamber notes that the Registrar has provisionally Exhibit Numbers P2338 to P2360 to the 23 associated exhibits which are currently marked for identification. The Chamber observes that 20 of these exhibits are photographs, one is a chart depicting disturbed and undisturbed Srebrenica primary graves, highlighting those worked on by the witness, and one is a table listing the different nationalities represented in the forensic teams in Srebrenica. The remaining exhibit is an autopsy report. Given the content of these associated exhibits, the Chamber considers it appropriate to admit them despite their relatively large number. Exhibits P2338 to P2360 are hereby admitted into evidence. Good afternoon, Mr. Hogan. Apologies for continuing with other business when you entered the courtroom. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. May I invite to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hogan. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: There were two things that I wanted to note before the witness entered the room, which I'll do at the beginning of the next session as he is being brought in, but I would also just like to note for the Chamber that he has been provided a copy, which he has with him, of the map book that is it now in evidence as P3. I hope that is acceptable. The book is in its original form except that it has also been marked with the corresponding e-court pages on each page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No objections for that. Whom do I have to address? Mr. Lukic, no problems. Mr. Hogan, you will first be examined by Ms. Hochhauser. You'll find her to your right. And Ms. Hochhauser is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can you please put your full name on the record?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Barry Allan Hogan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, you have testified before in the Dragomir Milosevic and Karadzic trials; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And you have worked on other Sarajevo-related investigations or cases?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Which ones were those?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: The Stanislav Galic trial.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your current assignment at the ICTY is?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I'm an OTP investigator currently assigned to the case against Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, have you had an opportunity before coming here today to review your prior testimony in the Karadzic trial?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And did you find it both accurate and truthful?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And if asked the same questions today, would you give the same answers? And actually before you answer me, I'm being reminded that you I both need to pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And between answer and question.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the answer to your question is yes, I would answer the same way.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, with that, I would tender 65 ter 30304, which is relevant excerpts of investigator Hogan's testimony in the Karadzic trial as well as the nine exhibit associated to that testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, first, the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We do not object to the transcript, but, right now, we don't know which exactly nine exhibits go with this transcript. We didn't extract it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then start with the transcript. The transcript would receive, Madam Registrar, number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter 30304 will be P2380.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Associated exhibits, Ms. Hochhauser, could you assist Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The first is 65 ter 10441, which is -- the satellite photo of Trebevic is the description.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would the next be 12936? Then 19792. Or -- I'm --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- just consulting the list we received.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It is the -- as they're listed on the list. The only -- the only thing that I would note is, for example, 19792 is shaded in grey because what we're offering is a subset that's listed under 19792A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other change to the list of associated exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: As -- as sent around earlier this mourning with a revised description, assuming that's the one that the Chamber has in its possession --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I can't promise you that I have this morning's version. But the numbers are still the numbers although the description has been changed?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we go through them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we don't -- we do not have to. We do not have any objections to none of these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that Madam Registrar prepares a list on which all the numbers appear and then now with the new descriptions and provisionally assign numbers to them. We would then need nine numbers to be reserved, and we'll decide on admission and we'll admit them once we have received those numbers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't believe that I need to relay a detailed public summary of Mr. Hogan's evidence but I can just say that Mr. Hogan is an OTP investigator with knowledge of Sarajevo and the Sarajevo-related charged crimes in the indictment. And then if I may proceed to questioning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And his testimony deals with that experience.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could at this point just make a quick clarification to the record. The number assigned to 30304 would be P2379 as the next exhibit number. So P2380 can be used for the other associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then P2380 to the extent was ... or at least is admitted into evidence, that's the ... one second, please. I'm apparently making mistakes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't listen carefully enough. The excerpts of transcripts admitted are admitted under P2379 and not as earlier indicated, P2380. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Investigator Hogan, can you please tell us just briefly the source of your familiarity with Sarajevo and its environs.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I've performed dozens of missions or trips to Sarajevo in furtherance of the various cases that I've worked on, starting in early 1999 for the OTP and, prior to that, I had served as a short term of duty with UNPROFOR in Sarajevo in the summer of 1992. With the OTP, I conducted investigations for the Galic case and for the Dragomir Milosevic case, assisted with Perisic case and now with the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And are you familiar with the allegations of the specific incidents that are charged in the F and G schedules of the Mladic indictment?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now you describe in your prior testimony - now in evidence as Exhibit P2379 at e-court pages 7 through 12 - that you along with colleagues from the ICTY attended the locations of the Scheduled Incidents in the Karadzic case, took GPS readings, recorded video footage and took photographs which were turned into 360-degree photographs. Are those the same incident locations as charged in the Mladic indictment?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell the Chamber, please, when those videos and photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: The -- for the incidents which occurred between May of 1992 and August of 1994, those incidents were filmed and photographed in September 2001. For the incidents which occurred after August 1994, up until the Dayton Accord in November 1995, those incidents were filmed in June of 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And specifically as to the videos that you made with -- pertaining to charged scheduled -- excuse me, pertaining to charged incidents, can you tell us what the procedure was you engaged in making those videos with either the victim or witness of that incident?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes. The -- first of all, the purpose of the videos was to quicken or shorten the viva voce testimony of the witness in either the Galic case or the Dragomir Milosevic case. The trial team worked out a procedure with me that we would request the witness or the victim to meet us at a location close to where the incident was known to have occurred. I was not to coach the witness. I was not to -- or victim. I was not to rehearse the witness or victim but was only asked to -- was only to ask the witness or victim to show me certain things and not speak on camera. The purpose of these videos was not to -- was not to replace their testimony. It was to provide a visual aid to the participants of those trials to assist in understanding the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, during the -- during those videos, you also took GPS, readings which have been tendered as associated Exhibit 12936, and I'm going to ask you, have you had an opportunity to review the Sarajevo map book in evidence as P3?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And were your GPS co-ordinates used in the marking of the specific incidents on the maps in Exhibit P3, specifically at e-court pages 6, 8, 9, 11, 15, 17, 19, 23, 27, 32, 33, 36, 37, and 41, which are the close-ups of the grid maps with a dot indicating the incident location?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I believe my GPS readings were used to create those markings.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. And those GPS readings, to be clear, are based on the witness statement to you of where the location was?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Not so much a statement but a demonstration to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can you explain the purpose of the 360-degree photographs that were taken and the methodology used when they were taken?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: The staff photographer who accompanied me during the filming placed a tripod for his camera on the spot where the witness or victim indicated he or she had been standing at the time of the incident. There was a device on top of the tripod which enabled the camera to make an arc of, I'm guessing, 5 degrees at a time, until a complete circle had been made with digital photographs taken at each stop along this 360-degree arc. The -- the purpose of these 360-degree photographs was to orient the parties to where within the city this incident had taken place and to provide a line of sight or a visual presentation of what it was at the time that we did these filmings.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, you said that the -- that the camera was set up on the spot where the witness or victim indicated he or she had been standing. To be clear, in the case of a witness, did they -- were at the standing where the witness was standing or where, to the best of their approximation, the victim was standing?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I was not clear. Sorry. It was -- is where the victim was standing or was situated at the time of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, have you had the opportunity to review those 360-degree videos in regard to -- to Scheduled Incidents F1, 4, 9, 12, 13, and 16?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And do those accurately depict a 360-degree view from the vantage point of where it was indicated to you the victim was standing?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, at this point, Your Honours, I would like to tender 65 ter 00945C, which is the video -- the 360-degree video pertaining to incident F1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. May I take it that it's the assembled photographs, rather than a video?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, it's a 360-degree panorama that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which is not a video in itself because the picture doesn't move but the photographs are assembled and then you're able to look at them from every angle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are we going to see it today in the courtroom or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: We are going to see at least one or two of them in the courtroom. But not every single one of them is my intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about this one? Are we going to see this one or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Not unless you decide to show it to the witness or the Judges would like me to show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But that's exactly what I'm trying to raise. Why would I spend my time allocated to our cross-examination to explain their evidence. I think that it's a proper way for the Prosection to show us the evidence they want to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I think what --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not -- it's non-associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What the Prosecution intends to do is to give us examples of this material and present the material in electronic format for the remainder of the incident sites. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. As I think has been explained by the witness, the purpose is for the Chamber to be able to navigate around the 360-degree view. If -- if the Chamber would like, I can show each and every one of them, but it was my intention to only show one or two so that the Chamber can have a sense of how these images work and the Chamber will later have them during deliberations for its use to examine in the context of the rest of the evidence for each Scheduled Incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we decide on admission, we'll have -- we'll first look at your examples and then hear what the explanation with it is and then we'll decide on the 00945C as tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. Shall I put on the record the -- the -- the 65 ter numbers which would relate or wait until the end?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you show it, you could -- these are several 65 ter numbers assembled in 00945C or how does it work?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. 45C relates to F1. 45D relates to F4 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So the number --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: -- et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The letters are indicative for the incident covered by that -- so let's start with the one you wanted to show examples. Was it 00945C which you would use as an example or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I was actually going to begin with the incident that is titled F3, which is the 11 July 1993 shooting death of Munira Zametica while collecting water.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then -- and that's -- what number would that be?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: That is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 00945 and then?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- I'm sorry, Judge. The F3 is actually already in evidence as P1907 but it was one that I was going to use in the context of other questions about F3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, start with the one you wanted to show us. Tell us what the 65 ter number is and let's look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I guess I will go back and start with the F1 video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the F1 video has -- is not a video but --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. 360-degree photo of F1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that is under number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: C. Okay, we start with that one.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We would appreciate it very much if you could slow down a little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will slow down. I always have to remind the persons and I'm making the same mistakes myself. Let's have a look at 945C.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hogan, I'll ask Ms. Stewart, who has control of the 360-degree picture, as we speak about it in court to take us around, and as she is slowly taking us around the photo, if you can tell us what it is we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I assume everybody's got the same picture as I do. We just saw the front door, and that is F1, front door. The gate to Zagrici [phoen] Street is being viewed now. We're rotating around to look towards the south very quickly now. The neighbouring house blocks much of the view to the south. But if we could pause --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm going ask, yeah, her to stop right --

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: If we could pause there. To the right of the hanging bit of laundry that we see, and to the left of that upright pole, there's a view of distant terrain. That distant terrain is actually what they call Baba Stijena or grandmother rock. That's on the southern slope of Mount Trebevic and is the actual front line positions of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And, Investigator Hogan, baba rock is that the alleged shooting location as far as you know from -- from other evidence pertaining to F1?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could continue I guess to see the whole 360-degree view.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I should point out that the vegetation and construction of the neighbouring houses was done after the -- the growth of the vegetation and the construction was done after the war. So that this, unfortunately, does not depict the view at the time of the sniping incident. And, again, the wall of the house of the family whose daughter was -- was wounded in this incident. And we're now back at the entrance -- entrance door. And that is a complete 360-degree view.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, the alleged shooting locations -- alleged location of the victim --

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: -- in F1?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. If you -- if the view can be brought down just a little bit and to the right. And to the right. And just down -- just down as far as can we can go. This is -- I'm sorry, the camera is located where the little girl had been standing, and the reason I wanted to show this doorjamb is because there was further evidence and investigation that was done in relation to that doorjamb. But the camera tripod was placed where the witness indicated her daughter had been standing at the time that she was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say the witness indicated about her daughter, is the -- the witness you're referring to Fatima Pita and the daughter Anisa Pita?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry, I'm little off about when you would like me to tender these. Now shall I tender this or are we waiting for them all at the end?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that if you have another example which you would like to show to us, that we look at that first and that we then consider where we are, whether we are ready to decide and whether Mr. Lukic is in a position to further comment on or declare his position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't want to guide the Prosecution how to conduct their examination but is it possible that mark that Baba Stijena on this 360-angle photograph? What is use of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yeah. So I would say actually that -- how I had intended to go through these was to discuss them incident by incident, and if we would look at page 10 in e-court of P3, you would see -- if we could -- if we could turn to that for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Am I right or am I wrong that there is a 92 bis motion - I don't know whether we have decided on it already - where the witness indicates -- says something about front lines and Baba Stijena?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct. I believe it was the 17th -- your decision on the 17th which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Recently --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: -- just was rendered last week. There is also additional evidence in the map book that comes right out of the 360-degree picture as well as the video, and that's on page 10 of P3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And is my recollection correct that in this 92 bis decision that one of the associated exhibits was a picture with markings or at least related to the statement of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, correct. My recollection is that Mrs. Pita marked it and that that has been admitted, and you'll see also, Judge, that the same thing exists, a picture, this picture, with a marking on page 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But it is not this picture, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but let's -- let's -- we'll describe it for the -- could we have a look at it again and could we pan to where the -- today's witness said Baba Stijena is. I think to the left is the shortest route to it. Could we pan to the left. Is there any way we could move this one so that we have ... Pan to the left. Yes. Could we stop there. Witness, you referred to Baba Stijena being visible. I understood this to be, but please correct me when I'm wrong, that at the far distance we see a -- what seems to me a right house and just right of that, the almost highest wooded hill, is that what you referred to as being Baba Stijena or would it be to the left of the house, between the neighbouring house and that house in the far distance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- what was pointed out to me as Baba Stijena was to the right of that house, that white house with the red roof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And there, we would see more or less the top of a hill just left of what seems to be an isolated tree or whatever it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, does that -- then we know at least what the witness referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, if -- if the witness could be so kind and mark it for us. So tomorrow we can check it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that we cannot mark it here on this -- on this electronic version, I think. Or is that possible? I'm not aware -- I've never seen any markings. Could it still be -- at least, Mr. Lukic, now you have a clear indication as where it is, what the witness referred to. And we could still ask for a still to be printed out so that, if it would be provided to you later, that you have it to assist you in preparing for your cross-examination. Let's move on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question. utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may correct a previous misstatement about what was admitted pursuant to Fatima Pita, I too quickly agreed, Your Honour, based on my memory as well about a picture that was circled but I don't see that we -- that the picture was admitted. utterances.text: Yes. Most likely I have remembered this page of P3, which misled me perhaps as well. Mr. Lukic, sufficient information for ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only I don't see that fence. I don't know if it's from the same time. But also I need calculation. Is it Pita incident or Munir Zametica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the Pita incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Pita incident, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the little girl on the balcony of her house, if I remember the evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's where I think the Defence objected against who was at what positions as a possible contradiction in the evidence and the statement of the witness. Mr. Lukic, that was the position of the Defence there. And I think that's dealt with in the decision. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, sorry, can I direct you again to page 10 in e-court of what we were just looking at, of P3, and looking at the caption underneath the picture on the left-hand side of the screen, can you tell us is this from the 360-degree photo or is it from the video interview? Where you --

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: It could be either. I'm sorry, which -- they were -- they were done at the same time and they showed similar views so this could be either from the video or it could be from the 360-degree photo.

utterances.text: At least in the still, I read still from video interview with victim's father. So I assume it's from the video interview and not from the 360-degree picture.

utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The -- the only reason I ask the witness to identify because obviously our captions are not evidence without additional testimony so I thought I might try to clarify it through him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we can turn, please, to incident F3. And I'm sorry, excuse me, it's F -- F3. And if we can please look at the 360-degree picture that's already in evidence as P1907. utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Certainly. And if you go to the right, please. And obviously that's the bank of the -- the small Dobrinja river. utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And is that, to your knowledge, the alleged origin of fire for this incident?

utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And just for demonstration -- if we could -- sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, is it clear enough to you? It's already in evidence but where the white tower is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Being semi-blind I don't see it clearly but I saw some other pictures I think what this gentleman is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER

utterances.text: So, again, if we could please turn back to P3 in evidence, which is the Sarajevo map book, page 10 in the hard copy and page 14 in e-court. And I don't know ...

utterances.text: I wonder --

utterances.text: Can you tell us please, Mr. Hogan, on page -- on this page, it's page 14 of this exhibit in e-court, can you tell us where this still is taken from and what we're looking at here?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN

utterances.text: And the -- the -- the visible -- I don't know what the proper architectural name for it is, but the spire or structure that we see that's encased in scaffolding on the left, is that the tallest piece of the building when we see it on the right?

utterances.text: Three minutes still to go.

utterances.text: Well, I will begin anyway.

utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at two documents in succession and then I'll ask you questions about the two of them together.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could please see 65 ter 30305 on the screen, which is a document of the Army of the Republic of BiH, entitled: "Report of the intelligence organ on the deployment and the strength of enemy forces," and it's dated 2 October 1993. utterances.text: Yes, it was. That was earlier this year.

utterances.text: Is the church named in these two documents the same church as the one depicted in the photos on e-court pages 12 through 14 of P3 of the Sarajevo map book, the church that we've just been looking at?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.text: And 65 ter 30306 will receive number P2390.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is also admitted into evidence. We take a break now. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back in some 20 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness should not yet be brought into the courtroom. Mr. Groome, the Chamber was informed that you would want to raise a matter in the absence of the witness and about timing, scheduling.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Thank you for the opportunity to do so. Your Honours, this submission is in response to the decision that the Chamber announced yesterday with respect to Reynaud Theunens and it concerns the implications of that decision. The Chamber's decision had two parts. I will deal with them in in order. With respect to part 1 of the report of the Chamber stated at T17439: "The Chamber is inclined to deny admission of part 1 and that it," meaning the Prosecution, "should elicit any relevant matters related to this part during the examination of Mr. Theunens." First, the Prosecution maintains its view as to the importance of part 1 and requests that if this decision by the Chamber was reached without considering General Milovanovic's evidence last week at T16929, the Prosecution would ask the Chamber to reconsider its decision in light of it. General Milovanovic testified: "Since most of us had been trained in the JNA, we were familiar with those rules and regulations, and that's why it was decided that we should continue applying them in the Army of the Republika Srpska." The Prosecution requests that the Chamber reconsider whether something other than a wholesale rejection of this portion of the report would not be fairer and more appropriate. Further, the Chamber's decision that the Prosecution should lead the evidence of this admittedly large portion of the report introduces a number of practical problems for the Prosecution. First, doing so would require significantly more time than our estimate of two hours. The Chamber has given us less than a week to adapt and implement its decision. The schedule next week has been finalized and it is the last week before the Chamber takes a recess. There is simply insufficient time next week to conduct the examination the Chamber has directed the Prosecution to conduct. Mr. Theunens is an important and substantial witness. Given the fact that drafting an examination that elicits the most important evidence from part 1 will take some time and that there is insufficient time to do this next week, it is the Prosecution's intention to reschedule the evidence of Mr. Theunens. We will work with him to identify an alternative time for this evidence. Second, the Prosecution's case is 86 per cent completed. There are 16 witnesses remaining, and I have already apportioned the remaining 22 hours the Chamber gave us to present our case among those witnesses. I have asked Mr. Weber, who is dealing with Mr. Theunens, to give me an estimate of the minimum amount of time it would take to lead this evidence from part 1. The estimate is six hours in addition to the two hours we originally estimated. The Prosecution is therefore now making an oral application for the addition of six additional hours to the presentation of its case. With respect to the number of documents, I do want to make it clear that the Prosecution does not agree with the Chamber's characterisation that it has "completely ignored" the Chamber's guidance and refers the Chamber to our military submission filed on the 26th of July in paragraph 29. The Chamber in its guidance from the 29th of October said the following: "Furthermore, once a proposed expert witness's conclusions are challenged by the cross-examining party, the Chamber will also allow the calling party to tender certain underlying materials." The Defence in their written response to Mr. Theunens's report indicated that they contested all of it. Given the amount of material involved and the difficulty in assessing which documents become important as a cross-examination is proceeding, the Prosecution had identified a selection of documents which appear to be necessary given the Defence written submissions. However, the Chamber has asked us to reconsider our approach, and we have. In light of that, we request two things. First, that the Chamber hold a 65 ter hearing outside of court during which the Defence can identify with greater precision those portions of the report which it truly contests. The Prosecution considers that much of the report, particularly those parts related to military doctrine of the JNA and VRS may not ultimately be contested. We would ask that this conference be held as soon as possible so that we can further reconsider our approach to Mr. Theunens's evidence in an informed way. Second, we would ask that in keeping with the Chamber's guidance, that we be given an opportunity after the completion of Mr. Theunens's testimony to assess which of his conclusions have been challenged during cross-examination and which documents will be necessary for the Chamber to have sight of in order to deliberate on that portion of the report. And, further, that we also have an opportunity to do the same with respect to the Chamber's ultimate decision with respect to which, if any, portions of part 1 it admits into evidence. Thank you, Your Honours, for this opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Could I ask you one question. If Mr. Theunens would be rescheduled, would you have a plan B for next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We do not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No. We would try --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, we would carefully consider your requests. At the same time, I can't anticipate on whether it will be granted or not. And, if not, then, of course, the -- perhaps you should already, taking this possibility into account, see whether there's any way that could you use the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, with so many witnesses -- so few witnesses remaining, there's really a small pool of witnesses to call. Mr. Theunens, I believe, is either here now or will be here. If the Chamber requires us to call him next week, then -- then we will.

utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- I think that's problematic and certainly is something I have discussed and discussed at length, whether that was a possibility. I think it's not in this case. I would be happy to address the Chamber in greater deal about that.

utterances.text: Yes. I'm not inviting you to do so at this moment but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I could just briefly correct the record about something. When I played P1907, I misspoke as to the timing. And at this point it's my intention to continue to call up the 360-degree videos, unless -- I guess unless I have direction from the -- from the Chamber otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We asked you to take a few examples so that we would know better what it is about. Mr. Lukic, do you think that they all should be played or that they all should be put to the witness, where the system that was used is clear, that witnesses were shown the place where the victim would have been, a tripod was put there, and then a 360-degree photograph was made at a time where some changes may have existed in terms of vegetation or constructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know what to tell you now, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that is if you -- you can accept -- you can admit evidence looking at it in court and having an explanation. Well, we have an explanation for all of the evidence, how it was created. And earlier you said, Well, it's difficult for us. And I'm asking you whether you can now take a position, having looked at two clear examples, one, by the way, already in evidence on -- on how this material was produced. And, of course, the Chamber can then further, as with all documents, photographs, et cetera, we just look at them very carefully. We could do the same for the others. Unless there is some specific reason why they should be shown in court now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Our understanding, Your Honour, is that associated exhibits are fine to go without being presented because it's part of the statement or testimony as it was in this case. But, if it's non-associated exhibit, we think that it has to be used in the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, non-associated exhibits have been admitted very often even from the bar table. Ms. Hochhauser, any ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just -- I would say I think there has been a sufficient foundation laid for them to enter them as exhibits -- as non-associated exhibited through this witness. He is -- he addresses them in the 92 ter testimony that is now in evidence. He has addressed, as you said, the procedure for which each of them was taken. They're clearly marked what -- what incident they're related to. But should the -- should the Chamber feel that it's -- it would assist the Chamber's understanding of the evidence that I'm tendering to go through or that it would be a requisite to through each them, I'm prepared to do that. I don't think it's legally required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further specific reason why we should look at them instead of -- now in court instead of looking at them as we often do with evidential materials, that is, being part of the body of evidence and then to be -- we'll hear your cross-examination if necessary. If there's any specific one on which you would like to cross-examine then, of course, you're free to do so. But is there any specific reason why we could not just watch that as illustrative material to other evidence received, we received on the incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The specific reason, Your Honour, might be that -- my understanding is nothing is visible on the first one. On the first 360-degree picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there's a lot visible. A house, where the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But not the spot from which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- there might be a fire. There is nothing there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you see the spot that's visible. From where the Prosecution says it was fired. You don't see on that picture, I do agree with you, you don't see a gun there. But you see a lot on that picture. Whether it's enough is a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The claim was that it was mountain Trebevic. There was no mountain on that picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it was Baba Stijena, not Mount Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Part of Mount Trebevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that may be close to -- of course, we have seen other evidence on that. It's not in isolation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is our -- our position so ... thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say because you can't see anything on the first one, that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But anything but not all that is described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is overruled, Mr. Lukic. Therefore, 65 ter 00945C, Madam Registrar, would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the number would be P2391.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Could you list the other ones, Ms. Hochhauser, so that we decide on their admission as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes. 65 ter 09945D, as in David, is pertaining to incident F4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same objection, Mr. Lukic or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same objection. And I don't know, because we haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it was on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: It was provided to counsel along with all other disclosure related to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next number for 09945D will be P2392.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Next one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: The next one I would actually -- I would just note that the -- the one pertaining to F5 is already in evidence as P1920 and the next one the Prosecution is tendering is 09945E which pertains to incident F9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the number would be P2393.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the presumption that the same objection applies. The Chamber decides that it is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: One -- the following one is 65 ter 10443A which pertains to incident F11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the same objection is raised and hereby overruled. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be P2394, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: 10443B, which is the video for -- excuse me. The 360-degree picture for F12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same objection, I take it. Also overruled. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the number would be P2395.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the 360-degree picture is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: 10443C which relates to incident F13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same procedure, I take it. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P2396, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: 10443D which relates to incident -- Scheduled Incident F15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the assumption that the same objection applies and again is overruled. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be P2397, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And finally 10443E which pertains to incident F16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same assumptions. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P2398, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: So turning back to -- sorry, incident F4, which is the 3 September 1993 shooting of Nafa Taric and her daughter.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to page 16 of P3 in e-court. It's page 12 in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us, Mr. Hogan, do you recognise the area that's depicted in these photographs?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And can you tell us what -- what we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: This is the street where the -- Mrs. Taric showed -- excuse me for a minute. Pardon me. Showed me the location of the incident. These are photographs that she marked in court during her testimony, and I think if you look at number 2 on the left-hand side, left -- sorry. The photograph on the left-hand side of the page --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: That's the one marked number 1?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: That's the photograph number 1. That's approximately where we stood when we were doing the filming of her video and the 360-degree panorama.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm just going ask you if you can clarify that. So we're looking at the photograph number 1 and when you say that's approximately where we stood are you referring to some marking on -- on that photograph number 1?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. It was along the footpath there is a circle with the number 2 beside it in blue ink. Oh, I see in your e-court screen it doesn't show up very much. I'm looking at the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Is it possible to zoom in on the -- sort of rectangular -- the black rectangle with stripes through it. And just -- just right there is perfect. Can you see now? Are we able to see it in e-court?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: It's just -- you can see an X along the footpath and in the hard copy there is actually a number 2 just past the X along the footpath towards the background and that's approximately where we were standing.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us this -- this black rectangular construction that reaches from sort of sidewalk to sidewalk across the street in the picture or approximately sidewalk to sidewalk, can you tell us what that would indicate to you?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes. That's where she indicated that there had been sniping barricades erected during the war or present during the war, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, during your prior testimony that's currently in evidence, picture -- associated exhibit which still bears the 65 ter number 23174 you marked the location of Ozrenska Street. Could you tell us whether the blue dot that we see on the top of the ridge in the photo marked number 1 is consistent or inconsistent with where you would put the location of Ozrenska Street on this photo on page 16 of P3 in e-court?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, it runs along the top of the ridge where the blue dot is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to turn to incident -- Scheduled Incident F5 which is the 2 November 1993 shooting of Ramiza Kundo. And if we could turn, please, to page 18 of the same exhibit, P3, in e-court. It's page 14 on the hard copy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, Madam Hochhauser, is there anything we need to know about photograph number 2 on this page?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we can -- thank you, Judge. If we can go back to page 17 -- 16 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Investigator Hogan, can you tell us with any more specificity, please, what we're looking at in the photo marked number 2 and from what vantage point?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes. This is the reverse view of the incident site, again marked by Witness Nafa Taric in court. Again the black hash marks indicate the -- where the sniping barricades had been located during the war and this -- the photograph was taken from Ozrenska Street looking down to Aziza Sacirbegovic Street. And, I believe, if you look on photograph 1 again, there's a white house at the top of the ridge, the tallest house on the top of the ridge and that's approximately where this photograph number 2 was taken from.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'll continue to -- onto incident, sniping incident number 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And page 18 in e-court. But I would also while we're coming to page 18 in e-court just put on the record because it seems like an appropriate time in reference to F4 which I didn't have an opportunity to do before the witness entered, that obviously there's a lot of evidence through this witness that we aren't offering -- aren't tendering in reliance on the adjudicated facts and so that's -- pertains to all of these incidents and I want that to be clear on the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: So turning to page 18 in e-court and incident F5, can you tell us -- there's a circle, a red circle, on the top of the page. Can you tell us is the location that was indicated to you for incident F5 contained within that circle?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And if it's possible can we zoom in on it a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The -- the incident location that was indicated to me is within the circle. It's almost exactly in the centre of the circle.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And obviously the circles takes up more space than one individual person would on the photograph. Are you able to mark for us with further specificity within this circle where exactly the victim was located?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: With the Court's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you like an X in the location?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can we -- if we could zoom back out again, please. Oh, we can't?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is impossible if it is marked. If you don't need any more markings, this one could be stored and you could tender it and then you could zoom out again on the original one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: That's what I'd like to do. Because I'll tender this one and ask him to mark on a zoomed-out photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, no objections on this marked photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be? It's one page of P3 which you can -- we can admit this in isolation, isn't it, as marked now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. The marked photograph will be saved as it is separate from P3 and will receive number P2399.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Would you now look to go back to the original unmarked one or would you now start with the marked one and then -- but we can't zoom that out any further from this version, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: No. I would like to go back to the original page 18, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 18 of P3. I just repeated what you said, but perhaps that would not be the right --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I believe it is the correct -- it should be page 18 which is two -- two past this page.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, are you able to tell -- tell us looking -- looking at this photograph, page 18 in e-court of P3, where the field area of Bacici and, I'm going to mispronounce the second one so I'm going to spell it, B-r-i-j-s-c-e [sic] --

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: -- are?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes. Brijesce is the field at the bottom of the hill, if you continue down the hill from the red circle and across the road to where that modern-looking building is, that is Brijesce area, that big field.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could maybe draw a circle around it. Does that --

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I could. And in addition, Bacici is off the screen to the right. So this circled area is Brijesce, and Bacici is off the screen just to the right in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And you've just drawn an arrow. So that arrow would indicate that Bacici is just past that arrow --

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: -- but off the field of the photograph; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can I offer this into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this marked photograph will receive number P2400 -- no -- yes, P2400. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And specifically in relation to that -- that item of evidence that's just been offered, I would just draw the Chamber's attention to adjudicated fact 2263. Can we have associated exhibit, please, 65 ter 23176 on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And it's coming up, I -- this is a -- what will be coming up is a mark you -- a map you marked previously in relation to this incident, F5, when asked to mark the field from which the shooting originated. And I noticed actually in looking at it that it's a little difficult to discern at this point which is your marking with all of the colours on this map. So could you please indicate for the Court, describe to us, which is your marking of that field?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Right. It's in the top left portion of this image -- of this map image and I made a red circular figure, but it's an uneven circle because my hand was shaking at the time, and it's in -- just down to the left of the number 5, the red dot with the number 5 beside it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. Turning now to incident -- Scheduled Incident F9, the 26 June 1994 shooting of 16-year-old Sanela Muratovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 20 in the map book, P3, in e-court, please. It's page 16 in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And as it's coming up, I believe you'll see there's a text box on the upper right-hand corner which marks the school for the blind as the place indicated with a 1, and the place of F9 as the place indicated on the map with a 2.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us anything about the reliability of the -- of those markers of that caption?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: They are accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'll just wait for it to come up before I move on. Can we turn to the next page in this exhibit, please, of P3, page 21 in e-court. Actually, I'm sorry, while we still have page 20 up on the screen -- that's right. I'll go to 21. It's okay. Sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what is it we're looking at here. What -- what's -- what does this photo show?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: This photo shows the witness at the location where she was showing me where her friend had been shot, and in the background, circled in red is the corner of the -- the upper corner of the school for the blind.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And in this photograph, can you tell us specifically where the witness is -- well, withdrawn. Is this -- is this a still from the videos that you described earlier how they were taken?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: I believe this is a still from the video. It looks as if we were actually filming at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. And the -- the location that the -- the woman in this photograph is standing, can you tell us, was that her -- was that her estimation of where the victim was?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, have you -- have you yourself been inside the school for the blind?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can turn to the next page, which is page 22 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: As it comes up, the question I'll ask you when you can see it on the screen is -- there's a red circle on this page, in the middle of the page, and there's a caption that reads: "View from the school for the blind." Can you tell us whether this is indeed the view from the school for the blind and what that circle indicates to you? What was that -- the position of that circle around?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN
utterances.text: Yes. That red circle is the position where we just saw myself and the witness standing in the previous photograph where the sniping victim was at the time she was shot. And this does indicate accurately the view from the top left window from the school for the blind.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that we're at the time for the break. I know that I estimated about an hour and a half with this witness. I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My information was one hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I sent an e-mail -- we sent an e-mail either yesterday or the day before changing the estimation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could be.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: But in any case, I would expect actually to take perhaps five to ten minutes longer than that, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how much time would you, then, in your estimate still need tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Approximately half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Half an hour is granted for tomorrow. Then we'll adjourn for the day. And, Mr. Hogan, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether given already or still to be given tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, Friday, the 27th of September, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
